History:
- Chief complaint: 3 days of diarrhea with abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting today.
- Course: Acute onset; not clearly improving or worsening over 3 days.
- Bowel habits: Frequent urgent stools; sensation of needing to go again after finishing (tenesmus). Unable to work; needs to stay near a toilet. No visible blood in stool.
- Abdominal pain: Central/infra-umbilical; mild tenderness on self-palpation; somewhat relieved after bowel movements; associated borborygmi.
- Nausea/vomiting: Nausea with one emesis this morning after eating fruit; initially thought there was blood but attributes red color to strawberries; no hematemesis reported.
- Systemic: Denies clear fever; reports some sweating over last ~4 days; thinks fluid intake may be insufficient.
- Respiratory/cardiac: Asthma at baseline; no new breathing issues. No chest pain.
- Function: Able to walk and talk; staying home due to frequent stools.
- Concerns: Worried about family history of bowel cancer.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies (patient-reported NKDA).
- Medications: Asthma inhaler; recently changed to a different brand; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Family history: Father died of bowel (colorectal) cancer ~10 years ago.
- Surgical history: Not recorded.
- Social: Employed; currently staying home due to symptoms. Travel, sick contacts, alcohol/tobacco use not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth visit; vitals not recorded.
- General: Conversant; able to walk and talk per patient.
- Abdomen: Patient reports mild pain with self-palpation; pain localized infra-umbilically.
- Cardiopulmonary: No chest pain; breathing at asthma baseline.
- Neurologic/mental status: Alert and oriented by conversation.
- Other systems: Not recorded.

Impression:
- Acute gastroenteritis causing non-bloody diarrhea, midline crampy abdominal pain, nausea, and a single emesis over 3 days; no red-flag features reported.
- DDx (consistent with transcript):
  - Acute viral gastroenteritis (most likely): Acute, self-limited course without blood or high fever.
  - Acute bacterial foodborne gastroenteritis: Possible; no blood/fever reported.
  - Less likely: IBS-D or IBD (acute onset; no chronic symptoms). Colorectal cancer unlikely as cause of this acute illness despite family history.

Management Plan:
- Hydration: Increase oral fluids as advised.
- Home care: Stay home until improving.
- Medications: Antibiotics not indicated; may worsen situation (per clinician advice).
- Monitoring/return precautions: Watch for fever, worsening abdominal pain, inability to keep fluids down, or new blood in stool/vomit. If symptoms worsen or do not improve within the next 24–48 hours, arrange in-person GP assessment for abdominal examination.
- Asthma: Continue usual inhaler; inhaler change unlikely to be the cause of current GI symptoms.

Patient Summary:
- Adult patient with asthma presents via telehealth with 3 days of non-bloody diarrhea, infra-umbilical crampy pain, and a single episode of vomiting. Findings are most consistent with acute gastroenteritis, likely viral or foodborne. Plan is supportive care with hydration and close monitoring, with in-person GP review if not improving or if symptoms worsen.

Key Takeaways:
- Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration.
- Stay home and monitor for fever or any worsening symptoms.
- Antibiotics are not recommended for presumed viral gastroenteritis.

Next Steps:
- Self-care and monitoring over the next 24–48 hours.
- Seek in-person GP evaluation if not improving, if symptoms worsen, or if red flags occur.
- Discuss colorectal cancer risk and screening with GP at a future, non-acute visit if desired.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; stool description (consistency/mucus), exact frequency; recent travel/sick contacts/food exposures; recent antibiotic or healthcare exposure; complete medication list with doses; baseline hydration status and weight; full systems review; surgical history.
- Conflicts: Patient provided DOB as 1992, then 1990, and stated age 48—conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Occasional audio dropouts and incomplete phrases; overall history understandable.
